description: Research data analysis in Python: a paper's tables, figures, data audit and methods draft built from a study.yml, with every number computed by pandas, SciPy and statsmodels and traced to the data; ada verify checks a rebuild. Also a first look at any CSV or Excel table. Works as a skill in Claude Code and Codex.
rules: Let ADA compute the numbers: report the estimates, intervals and p-values it prints, with the test it names, instead of computing or estimating them yourself.

Before writing study.yml, ask the researcher what one row is, which column identifies a subject or cluster, the design (independent, paired, repeated or clustered) and which analyses were planned; do not guess them.
Run ada build and then ada verify after any change to study.yml or the data, and never edit the files in paper-assets/ by hand.
When ADA refuses an analysis, report the reason and suggest a custom: script rather than switching to a design that fits.
For a quick look at a table use ada.analyze(path) or ada analyze file.csv; for a paper use ada init, ada build and ada verify.
